name: Victoria
landscapeNotes: The tree bylaw gives extra protection to trees on slopes steeper than 33 per cent and within 15 m of a watercourse, so steep or creekside lots need a check before work.

localRules.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

Victoria's Tree Protection Bylaw protects private trees over 30 cm diameter at breast height, hedges with any stem over 30 cm, Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific yew and Pacific dogwood over 50 cm tall, replacement trees, and trees on steep slopes or near watercourses. A permit may be needed to prune, remove or work in the root zone of a protected tree.

The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

name: Saanich
landscapeNotes: Saanich's bylaw names Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood and Pacific yew as protected at small sizes, and also protects trees with raptor, osprey or heron nests, so native-tree and nesting checks belong in any pruning or removal plan.

Saanich's Tree Protection Bylaw protects Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood and Pacific yew at 2 m tall or 4 cm diameter; Douglas-fir, grand fir, bigleaf maple and western redcedar at 30 cm diameter; any other tree at 60 cm; plus replacement, significant and nesting trees. A tree cutting permit is required before cutting a protected tree, even if dead or dying, and the bylaw also covers pruning or damaging protected trees.

The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. propertyTypes: industrial and commercial sites in Keating
landscapeNotes: Central Saanich has an Erosion District where removing any tree needs a permit and a geotechnical engineer's report.

Central Saanich protects dogwood, arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific yew, shore pine and trembling aspen, nesting trees, permit-retained trees and any tree over 0.6 m diameter. Pruning or removing a protected tree needs an application with a site plan (an arborist report may be required); removing any tree in the Erosion District needs an Engineering permit and geotechnical report.

The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. North Saanich's Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1548 requires a permit to remove any regulated tree (generally 20 cm diameter or more, smaller for arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific dogwood, yew and shore pine, plus trees in environmental or steep-slope areas). Topping is prohibited; best-practice pruning needs no permit. Staff review takes about 2-3 weeks and the permit must be posted 48 hours before work.

name: Highlands
landscapeNotes: Highlands requires a tree cutting permit for any tree near a watercourse, lake or steep slope, so many rural lots need a check before clearing.

localRules.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply (many rural properties use wells; the rules apply only where connected): lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

Under Highlands' Tree Management Bylaw No. 10, cutting a protected tree (Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood, Pacific yew, cascara, manzanita, Douglas-fir over 60 cm, any tree over 80 cm) or any tree near a watercourse, lake or steep slope needs a permit; cutting a significant tree is prohibited. Check for nesting birds before felling in nesting season.
